verdicts.flaw_description: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A new insert grade shortens cycle time on its own, and all four March runs were cut on those machines, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

Two of the four cases have the measurement before the intervention: case One was "issued 4 November" but scored "by 27 September", and case Three was "issued 5 June" but scored "by 28 April" (the term labels conflict too - an autumn-term section read out in September). Half the evidence therefore records completion gains that predate the kit.

The numbers cover a narrower population than the claim: "Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices." Roughly 20 percent of each line's post-change orders are dropped from the after-figure while the "month earlier" baseline is the whole line, so the 4-7 percent lift is a selected subset, not the line's revenue per order.

The absence figures are restricted to a self-selected subgroup: they "cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable." That fifth is excluded from the after-figure but included in the "term earlier" cohort baseline, so the 4-7 percent drop compares a filtered set of pupils against the full cohort.
